question: What does the source's fixed keyword-decryption and rearrangement grid produce on the actual ten rune streams read by its program?
target_mapping: Source pages/page_21 through page_30 are global image ordinals and match current LP2-04 through LP2-13 exactly by GP rune sequence; they are not current LP2-21 through LP2-30.
source_methods: Run every operator invoked by solve_page: source keyword-column variants, all permutations when keyword-character count <=7, two 25-position magic-square directions, listed plain column widths, spiral/snake/rail/diagonal widths, prime extraction, every-nth routes, reversal, two keyword+magic compositions where eligible, and no-transposition baseline. Preserve source code, source scoring, ties and source order.
source_scoring: The archived combined_score on continuous GP runeglish; its word scorer sees an unbroken string, so ordinary word matches cannot be inferred from that score. No substitutions, whitespace reconstruction or new language model.
positive_controls: Independently check route permutation length/multiset, forward/reverse round trips where claimed invertible, and a planted known-message keyword-column route. Record source functions that fail their own claimed inversion rather than silently fixing them.
limitations: The source keyword assignments are proposals, not verified LP2 decryption keys; source documentation advertises methods not actually invoked. A best score is a ranked candidate, not a reading. Other four scripts in this cohort use different scorers or absent external inputs and are audited separately.
